days.title: Whitesands Bay and St Davids Head
days.description: A short, dramatic opener on the tip of the peninsula

activities.activity: Walk the coast path loop from Whitesands Bay around St Davids Head
activities.notes: 6 km loop past the Coetan Arthur burial chamber — seals often haul out below

activities.activity: Visit St Davids Cathedral and settle into the city

days.title: Porthgain to Abereiddi and the Blue Lagoon
days.description: Industrial heritage and the famous flooded slate quarry

activities.activity: Take the Strumble Shuttle to Porthgain and walk the cliff path to Abereiddi
activities.notes: Bus approach — 5 km of the path's best cliff scenery

activities.activity: Lunch above the Blue Lagoon and watch the coasteering groups

days.title: Solva to St Davids via Caerfai

activities.activity: Walk the coast path from Solva harbour to Caerfai Bay
activities.notes: 10 km of switchback headlands — the toughest walking of the week

activities.activity: Descend to Caerfai Bay for a swim if the sea allows, then up to St Davids

days.title: Marloes Sands and the Deer Park
days.description: A farewell circuit at the island end of the coast

activities.activity: Drive south to Marloes and walk the Marloes Sands circuit
activities.notes: Transfer by car (40 min), then an easy 8 km loop

activities.activity: Round the Deer Park headland at Martin's Haven for Skomer views
activities.notes: Puffin season on Skomer — add the boat crossing if you have a spare morning

finalText:
Here's your 4-day Pembrokeshire Coast Path plan, based in St Davids: day 1 the Whitesands and St Davids Head loop to find your legs, day 2 the Strumble Shuttle out to Porthgain for the cliff path to Abereiddi's Blue Lagoon, day 3 the classic Solva-to-St Davids stage via Caerfai (your biggest day at 10 km), and day 4 the Marloes Sands circuit with the Deer Park headland and Skomer views to finish.

On conditions: I tried to pull the typical early-May figures for Pembrokeshire, but the weather lookup is unavailable right now, so I couldn't retrieve historical data — and I'd rather tell you that than invent numbers. What I can say from the character of the place: early May on the Welsh coast is usually mild but changeable, with real wind on the headlands and a decent chance of showers, so pack a windproof shell, and the wildflowers on the clifftops are at their absolute best. I can try the lookup again shortly and give you proper figures.

On cost: guesthouses in St Davids run about £70–£90 a night in May, and the coastal shuttle buses are a couple of pounds per hop, so budget roughly £450 per person for the four days with meals. Want me to adjust the pacing or add the Skomer boat crossing?
